messages:
Anne: Quick sync — Novatech is ready to run a lightweight sweep next Tue 09:00 PT. Goal: validate perf-per-watt change after their kernel patch + our 8-bit quant profile. Can folks confirm telemetry tagging and run command?

Kai: I can take the run. Need exact model, seq len, and the batch schedule you want. Also confirm whether to enable KV-cache warmup.

Anne: Model we'll use: redwood-mini-13B-8bit (this is the verified 8-bit recipe). Seq=1024. KV-cache=on, warmup=200 tokens, batch plan: 1 warmup stream at batch=4, then steady-state batch=2. Telemetry tag: novatech-ignite-1. Rollout window Tue 09:00-11:00 PT.

Sophie: Added to calendar and created a short run channel. Invite Novatech-eng and telemetry-bot. I've put a 30m retro right after.

Raj: I'll own rollback coordination with Novatech if we see regressions. Novatech, can you confirm BMC/PMU access method and wattmeter type (IPMI vs external meter)? We'll need that before Tue.

novatech-eng: Confirmed — we'll provide IPMI for BMC counters and an external Yokogawa wattmeter on the primary rail. We'll drop creds into vault with access for Kai and Raj. We'll also attach a kernel patch branch name: hw/patch/perf-2026-ignite.

Kai: Copy. Run command I'm going to use:

```bash
./run_sweep \
  --model redwood-mini-13B-8bit \
  --seq_len 1024 \
  --batch_warm 4 \
  --batch_steady 2 \
  --warmup_tokens 200 \
  --kv_cache on \
  --telemetry_tag novatech-ignite-1 \
  --output run.json
```

Kai: Telemetry knobs: sample_interval=1000ms for watt, cpu/gpu counters at 250ms, and perf PMU counters at default. We'll collect dmesg + perf.data after each run.

telemetry-bot: Scheduled run object created -> https://telemetry.internal/runs/2239998888. Data sinks: s3://redwood-telemetry/partnerships/novatech/ignite-1/

Sophie: Can we also enable a light kernel trace on the first warmup stream only? Just to catch anomalies.

Raj: Yes — enable ftrace for the warmup and then disable for steady-state to avoid noise. I'll add the script to toggle. Also make sure power cap is set to 300W for node-1 and node-2 to keep runs comparable.

novatech-eng: We'll prep the nodes, apply hw/patch/perf-2026-ignite to the test lane, and set power cap. We'll also validate thermals on a short smoke run Fri afternoon.

Kai: Quick note on metrics calculation — we'll measure tokens/sec (decoded tokens) and average watt over steady-state window. Perf/W = tokens_sec / avg_watt. Postprocessing script:

```python
# calc_eff.py (very small)
import json, csv
with open('run.json') as f: r=json.load(f)
# r contains samples: timestamps, tokens, watt
# compute steady window average and tokens/sec -> write metrics.csv
```

Anne: Expected artifacts we want attached after the run: run.json (telemetry), perf.data, kernel dmesg, ftrace snippet (warmup), and a short notes.md with any anomalies. We'll use those artifacts for the joint results brief.

Sophie: I'll own the joint brief draft (template in drive) — aim to have first draft within 24h of the run.

Raj: Also add a small acceptance gate: if perf/W drops by >6% vs baseline we pause and investigate before any public statements. If regressions are minor (<2%), we note them.

novatech-eng: Understood. We'll run internal smoke and share baseline numbers by EOD Monday.

Kai: One last thing — kernel revert procedure (in case):
1) mark the build as bad in CI
2) revert hw/patch/perf-2026-ignite branch on test lane
3) re-run the warmup smoke
4) notify Anne/Sophie/Raj

Anne: Sounds good. Anything else?

Sophie: Nothing from me. See you Tue 09:00 PT — please be in the partner channel 10 min early. :thumbsup:

telemetry-bot: Reminder set -> Tue 08:50 PT.

novatech-eng: All set from our side. Sending vault link now. Thanks everyone!
